intro: A country singer from the Pickathon family.
story: Caleb Klauder, a Portland mandolinist and singer and a founding member of the old-time Foghorn Stringband, played Pickathon in 2007, one of three visits that also took in 2001 and 2013. He fronts his own Caleb Klauder Country Band, playing original songs in an old-style country vein. He and Reeb Willms released the duo album Oh Do You Remember in 2012 and Innocent Road, 14 originals, in September 2016, and the country band's third album, Gold in Your Pocket, came out on Free Dirt Records on November 15, 2024.
artist_reel_line: Gold in Your Pocket, his country band's third album, came out in November 2024.

intro: A Portland bluegrass quartet with a honky-tonk edge.
story: Jackstraw, the Portland bluegrass quartet, played Pickathon in 2001, 2003, 2005 and 2007, and returned in 2009, 2013 and 2022. Their self-titled album came out in 2003 and Live at the White Eagle, recorded in September 2004, in 2005. Sunday Never Comes, their sixth album, arrived in April 2012 with banjo player Cory Goldman.
artist_reel_line: Sunday Never Comes, their sixth album, came in 2012 with a new banjo player.

story: Little Country Giants, a Georgia Americana quartet, are led by the husband-and-wife duo of Russell and Cameron Cook, from Oakman in the foothills of northwest Georgia, who play vintage Southern folk, bluegrass and country. They played Pickathon in 2007. By January 2010 Fists of Foam and Fury was being reviewed and a fifth CD was in the works.
artist_reel_line: Fists of Foam and Fury was reviewed in January 2010, with a fifth CD in the works.

story: Flat Mountain Girls, a Portland old-time string band with Lisa Marsicek on fiddle, Rachel Gold on banjo, Nann Alleman on guitar and Arthur Parker on bass, played Pickathon in 2007, the year their third album, Idle Talk & Wicked Deeds, came out on May 23. Honey Take Your Whiskers Off came in 2005. No Depression profiled them as postmodern traditionalists and called the new album a perfect distillation of the band. It became a local favorite on the Northwest square-dance and festival circuit.
artist_reel_line: The band became a favorite on the Northwest square-dance circuit.

intro: A Portland band of punk-fueled jug-band blues.
story: Sassparilla, a Portland band of punk-fueled jug-band blues, played Pickathon in 2007 and again in 2008. The double album Pasajero and Hullabaloo came out in June 2014, and Honey, I'm Using Again, written in a basement in Golden, Colorado, followed on In Music We Trust in 2026.
artist_reel_line: Honey, I'm Using Again came out on In Music We Trust in 2026.

intro: A witty swing duo of upright bass and tenor guitar.
story: Andy Bean and Fuller Condon began as a busking act in New York's Central Park in 2005 and released their self-titled debut that year. The Two Man Gentlemen Band, a swing duo of upright bass and tenor guitar, followed with Great Calamities in 2006, Heavy Petting in 2008 and Drip Dryin' in May 2009 on Serious Business Records. They played Pickathon in 2007 and again in 2012, the year NPR's World Cafe named them its Next artist on the rise. They composed the theme for Disney's Wander Over Yonder in 2013, and Bean was nominated for an Annie Award for the music.
artist_reel_line: NPR's World Cafe named them its Next artist in 2012; Disney used their theme in 2013.

story: Gregory and the Hawk is Meredith Godreau, a New York singer-songwriter who took the name in 2003, after her brother and his imaginary hawk. Her full-length debut, In Your Dreams, came out in 2007 on Pearly Gates, which led to a deal with Fat Cat Records, and she played Pickathon that year as her delicate songs were finding an online audience. Fat Cat released Moenie and Kitchi in 2008, which became a cult favorite, and Leche in 2010.
artist_reel_line: Fat Cat released Moenie and Kitchi in 2008 and Leche in 2010.

intro: A Texas-raised songwriter with Pacific Northwest ties.
story: Raina Rose, born in Los Angeles and raised in Portland, moved to Austin in 2007, the year she played Pickathon with clear, expressive folk songs. She recorded solo albums in Portland between 2006 and 2009, then When May Came in 2010 and Caldera in 2013, her fifth. Vesta came out on Folk Potions in January 2020. After years of touring and time away to raise a family, she returned with the community-funded album Afterglow in 2025.
artist_reel_line: Afterglow, a community-funded album, came out in 2025.

intro: Austin's hard-charging honky-tonk and bluegrass outfit.
story: The Weary Boys formed in Austin in 2000, when Mario Matteoli, Darren Hoff and Brian Salvi left Humboldt County, California to play bluegrass and country as a string band. The Austin Chronicle counted them among the city's best alt-country bands until 2007, the year they played Pickathon, just before a long break from the road. The members reunited for shows in 2013, and DARKHORSE, a new album, came with Texas club dates in late 2026.
artist_reel_line: DARKHORSE, a new album, came with Texas club dates in late 2026.
